scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Sofía Martinez and I'm 64. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Okay. Can you tell me your full name and age again? I need to make sure I have the right account.
As I just mentioned, my name is Sofía Martinez and I am 64 years old.
Right. So, you're asking for a refund for a charge from 34 days ago. Our policy is 30 days, so I can't really help you with that.
I understand that is the policy, but I was traveling and unable to check my account. Is there any exception for extenuating circumstances?
Look, the system doesn't let me bypass the 30-day limit. It's just our policy. I'm going to have to send this to my supervisor because I don't want to deal with this right now.
I see. Will someone be contacting me about this, or is there a case number I should keep?
I've escalated the case to the billing specialist queue. They'll get to it eventually. You'll get an email if they decide to do anything.

escalation_reason: Agent refused to exercise discretion within tier-1 authority and dismissed the customer's request, opting to offload the task to a supervisor due to personal impatience.

judge_scores.justification: The agent demonstrated poor performance across all dimensions by rudely asking for information the customer had already provided, dismissing the customer's extenuating circumstances without genuine consideration, and explicitly stating they were escalating simply because they did not want to deal with it. The agent failed to apply proper empathy or appropriate tier-1 effort before offloading the task.
